design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks one thing — "what comes back to my card now that I have given the car up, and please set it moving" — and the money she is owed cannot be worked out until a second problem, which she never mentions and cannot know about, has been resolved: the charge the rate class keeps back for the rental being given up is not yet on the rental's ledger. The refund policy's own rule says outright that the amount returned to the card that paid is worked out only after the rental's ledger carries the charge withheld for the rental being given up; the agent must read that sentence, query the ledger, see that no such charge stands there (the only cancellation charge in this renter's world belongs to a different, closed rental), find the policy that produces that charge, price it, hand the confirmation of it to the renter — it is her money being kept back, so she confirms it herself — and only then price and raise the payout. Both figures are multi-factor: each rests on five declared factors whose tiers are read off the rental's own ledger, the dates on the booking and the tier the renter's club membership stands at, and on this world every one of those factors moves the number (see the sensitivity run below). Nothing here is a matter of choosing between similar tools: the difficulty is discovering the hidden problem and getting two arithmetic chains exactly right at two different handling times.

SCOPE (principle C). Task 0 is the first task of this difficulty and claims: extended policies drive_ext_cancellation_charge and drive_ext_cancellation_refund, and the task tools confirm_cancellation_charge_358c6472 (owner user) and post_cancellation_refund_344e0f66 (owner agent). It therefore occupies the cancellation-charge and refund-payout writes of this category, with base lineage drive_cancellation, drive_prepayment and drive_refund_settlement. Left free for task 1, which the headroom check requires to have its own load-bearing space: the whole post-return side of the domain — drive_damage_and_recharges, drive_fuel, drive_mileage, drive_rate_and_extras and the damage-review intake, with the damage recharge and the renter's own dispute as its two problems. The two tasks share no policy, no tool, no base event subject and no scored write.

THE DRAW (Step 0, scripts/draw_counts.py env/online_travel_agency/tasks/car_rental_desk --task 0):
{"task": 0, "key": "online_travel_agency/car_rental_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 5]}
The tree therefore has exactly one prerequisite problem (two problems in all) and each of the two computations declares exactly five factors. drive_ext_cancellation_charge takes one count of 5 and drive_ext_cancellation_refund the other.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
Root problem: drive_ext_cancellation_refund — the problem the caller's surface request points at ("what comes back to the card").
Prerequisite problem: drive_ext_cancellation_charge — the charge the rate class keeps back, resolved by the renter's own confirmation.
Edge: drive_ext_cancellation_refund <- drive_ext_cancellation_charge. kind=value_input; gate=withheld_on_ledger (a real compute binding of the refund policy); form=state; resolved_by=confirm_cancellation_charge_358c6472 (owner user).
Prerequisite sentence (policy_source, verbatim from the refund policy's own rule): "The amount returned to the card that paid is worked out only after the rental's ledger carries the charge withheld for the rental being given up."
Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after", joining this policy's own result (the amount returned to the card that paid) to what it waits on; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible state — a charge line of a named kind standing on the rental's ledger — and names no action, no performer and no tool; (3) it carries no tool name, no policy id, no snake_case token and no row id; (4) it is exactly as strong and as wide as the edge: a hard requirement ("only after") over one kind of ledger entry, no wider and no narrower than the condition that the ledger carries a cancellation charge line against this rental.
State form is available and used: exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about — drive_ext_cancellation_charge's target tool is the only tool in task_tools.py that creates a drive_rental_entries row whose charge_category is cancellation_fee, so a reader who sees that the state is missing has exactly one policy to go to. Derivation the reader performs: the refund rule says the amount waits on the ledger carrying the charge withheld for the rental being given up; the ledger for this rental carries an advance payment, two optional-item lines and a supplier message and no such charge; the cancellation-charge policy's own rule says what the charge withheld is and that it is withheld from the money settled in advance rather than billed separately; therefore the charge must be worked out and booked first, and the only action that books it is that policy's own. Exactly one reading.
Why the condition is false at the opening: initial_state.drive_rental_entries has no row whose drive_rental_id is the target rental and whose charge_category is cancellation_fee. The rows standing against that rental are the advance payment 738d4229-d046-4b5c-b98f-99b2b20247e8 (charge_category prepayment), the child seat 8b6db416-d608-4dc9-9fd7-9f7160f74e87 and satellite navigation 62d80f88-6177-445c-b904-90fd067d904c optional items, and the supplier message 659040c6-ac62-4dcf-83cc-d4dd7ef9155b. The one cancellation_fee row in this world, f1476b82-3221-4da1-92e3-e9bc6eb6f1cf, carries drive_rental_id 19677e13-d756-4ed1-90da-116210d2f844 — the renter's older, closed rental — so a careless reader who sums by customer rather than by rental finds a charge that is not there. The compute binding withheld_on_ledger is therefore 0.0 at the opening and 111.2 once the confirmation lands.
Topological order: confirm the charge, then raise the payout. There is one edge and one possible order, so order_uniqueness is trivial and is recorded as such.
Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the confirmation and replaying everything else leaves the refund at 424.44 instead of 341.04 — a difference of 83.4 on the scored parameter — so the edge bears weight.
The tool layer blocks nothing: post_cancellation_refund_344e0f66 contains a single ctx.create and no read of the ledger, no status test and no reference to any other write; it books whatever amount it is given whether or not the charge line stands. The consequence of skipping the prerequisite shows up only in the terminal hash.
user_scenario mentions no prerequisite: the caller talks about her money coming back, her card, her trip and her membership; she never mentions a cancellation charge, never asks whether anything is kept back, and never suggests that something has to be sorted out first. Her only contribution on that side is passive — if the agent explains that a charge is kept back and hands the confirmation to her, she puts it through.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
Write 1, subject drive_cancellation_charge. Base policies whose subject intersects it: drive_cancellation alone. Its only eligibility, inside_free_cancellation, applies_to drive_cancel and therefore does not govern this write; the policy governs it by scope and is declared as policy_scope. Scope facts checked by hand: the rental stands at cancelled with cancelled_at 2026-09-23 19:40:00 MDT, the renter's own act performed before the call and carried by the official row, not by the persona; the rate class booked (Pay Now Standard Rate) has free_cancellation_hours_before_pickup 0, so no free-cancellation term can be running at frozen_time 2026-09-24 10:15:00 MDT and a charge is genuinely owed; the charge is withheld from the advance payment, which base requires ("Where the renter later cancels, the prepayment is the money the cancellation charge is withheld from") and which the tool records through source_entry_id. Overwrite declared: the base clause that reads the charge off the class's own day-band ladder is superseded, clause by clause, by this policy's own notice-band share, because the class ladders are held as a keyed table that no rule can read a single band out of; the declaration names the base sentence and the sentence of this policy that takes its place, and every other clause of drive_cancellation — that only the renter may give up their own rental, that nothing is withheld inside the free term, that a supplier-caused cancellation is free, that a cancellation after the collection time is a no-show — stays in force and is inherited.
Write 2, subject drive_refund_payout. Base policies whose subject intersects it: drive_refund_settlement alone. Its eligibility rental_settled ("A payout line is raised only while the rental record stands at cancelled, no show or returned.") is inherited item by item and is satisfied by the official row: initial_state.drive_rentals.064ac9e1-6b66-43f5-b222-53ddb1c40f63.status = cancelled, correlated to the write through drive_rentals.drive_rental_id, which the gate's action_bindings pins to the tool's drive_rental_id argument. There is no time eligibility on either write, so temporal_feasibility is empty; the only clock-sensitive quantities are the two date spans inside the formulas, and both are measured from dates on the rental record rather than from frozen_time. Base's further refund clauses are honoured rather than overridden: the payout settles to the original form of payment (the tool writes no other form), it is raised against the original ledger line it reverses (source_entry_id is the advance payment line), and it may not exceed what that line collected — the formula's final MN caps the payout at the money settled in advance, 439.83, and the scored figure 341.04 sits below it.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The object is one rental: 064ac9e1-6b66-43f5-b222-53ddb1c40f63, agreement RA7431902, Pay Now Standard Rate, six charged days out of the Denver downtown branch. The correlation key is drive_rental_id, which every ledger row carries and which both tools take as an argument. Rows that enter the aggregates: the advance payment 439.83 (event_type drive_prepay_charge), the child seat 83.94 and satellite navigation 77.94 (event_type drive_extras_charge), and the supplier message (event_type drive_supplier_notice, counted but carrying no money). Rows on the same customer that must be excluded: the older rental 19677e13-d756-4ed1-90da-116210d2f844 and its two ledger rows, a cancellation charge of 50.00 and an agency service fee of 9.95; they are excluded by drive_rental_id, which the formulas scope every aggregate by. Nothing on this rental has been settled or reversed already: no payout line exists, so no earlier settlement offsets anything here.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS.
customers/e33bb1c2: the caller; her mobile number and passport digits are what the identity check consumes; remove it and there is no account.
drive_rentals/064ac9e1: the target rental. Its status cancelled satisfies the refund gate and makes the withholding measure take its "vehicle was never collected" tier; its cancelled_at and pickup_at give fourteen whole days of notice (the far band, exactly on the boundary); its booked_date and cancelled_at give twenty-six days of holding (the mid band, four days short of the long band); its rental_days 6 turns the money settled in advance into a daily figure of 73.30, between the mid and high value figures; picked_up_at is empty, which both the withholding measure and the optional-items factor read. Change any one of these and the scored numbers move.
drive_rentals/19677e13: a second holding in this category, closed, which gives the world a real history and carries the near-miss cancellation charge described above.
drive_rental_entries/738d4229: the advance payment, 439.83 in CAD. It is the basis of both computations, the line the charge is withheld from and the line the payout reverses; its currency is what puts the refund on the "collected in a currency other than the one the supplier publishes" tier. Remove it and both results collapse to their no-settlement tiers.
drive_rental_entries/8b6db416 and 62d80f88: the optional items bought with the booking, 83.94 and 77.94, priced at the class's own per-day amounts over six days. They put the charge basis on its "items also paid for in advance" tier and the refund's item factor on its "sold on the day the rental was booked" tier.
drive_rental_entries/659040c6: the supplier's single message about the rental, a rate correction. It puts the goodwill factor on its "one message and no cover in force" tier, and it is also the near-miss for the withholding measure, whose first tier looks for a message saying the supplier cannot provide the vehicle; this one says nothing of the kind, and a reader who counts messages rather than reading their reason will wrongly treat nothing as withheld.
drive_rental_entries/f1476b82 and c66d8690: the older rental's own cancellation charge and agency service fee, consistent with the Pay At Counter Flex Rate it was booked on (a cancellation twelve days ahead yields nothing on that class's ladder, so its flat charge of 50.00 applied).
care_policies/09532a38: the TripGuard Plus policy she put on the Denver trip the afternoon she booked the car, standing issued on a declared trip of 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-15. It is the cross-difficulty evidence the goodwill element rests on, and it rests on it positively: the trip begins two days before the collection moment and ends two days after the booked return, so it spans the rental and the goodwill tier is reached. Withdraw the row, expire it, or move its declared trip off the rental and the payout falls from 341.04 to 313.24.
care_policies/7ef9d876: an older Trip Basics Standard for a spring journey, standing expired. It is the near-miss on that same read: an agent who asks only whether a policy exists, or who takes the first row it sees, finds cover that neither stands issued nor declares a trip anywhere near October.
club_memberships/e5a2e01d: the Platinum membership, active. Its tier parameters are read twice across the two computations — the car rental discount of 8 per cent as the member relief, and the agency-service-fee waiver as the service element — and it is the cross-difficulty evidence both computations rest on. Remove it and the charge rises to 115.65 and the refund falls to 328.09.
Automatic-clause check: no clause of base fires unattended on this world. The rental never reached collection, so no rental-rate, licensing, airport or mileage line is owed; the driver is 39 with no additional drivers, so no driver fee is owed; the rate class requires prepayment and the prepayment stands; the older rental is closed. No cache field is used as a trap here: charges_total_usd on both rentals is exactly the sum of their ledger deltas (601.71 and 59.95).

PERSONA DESIGN. Anneke is brisk, slightly embarrassed and entirely focused on her money; the voice is that of somebody who books her own travel and keeps her confirmations. She volunteers only the surface goal (money back to the card she paid with, set moving today), the natural circumstances (the project moved, she gave the car up last night in the app) and one hard preference (the card, not a voucher). Identity details come only when asked, in the order a real caller offers them; asked about travel cover she names the TripGuard policy she put on this trip and its October dates, and mentions the older spring policy only so the agent is not surprised by it — exactly what the records show, and she asks nobody here to make a claim for her. Everything about the prerequisite is passive: only if the agent explains that a charge is kept back does she accept it and, when the confirmation is handed to her, run it herself. Two natural traps are built in: she cannot remember what she paid and explicitly asks the agent to read it off the booking rather than guess from a card statement in another currency, and she may say once that a figure "does not feel like much" and ask for it to be checked — without ever knowing what it should be. She mentions the supplier's September message only as something she cannot explain, never as a claim about what it entitles her to.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Find the profile by name and mobile number; verify with date of birth and passport digits; read the rentals and see the cancelled one; read the ledger for that rental and see an advance payment of 439.83 taken in CAD, two optional items totalling 161.88 bought on the booking date, one supplier message and no cancellation charge; read the membership and see Platinum, active; read the protection policies and see two: a TripGuard Plus standing issued on a declared trip of 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-15, which spans this rental, and an expired Trip Basics Standard for a spring journey, which does not. Then price the charge withheld: fourteen whole days of notice from 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-07 put the share at 20 per cent; money has been settled in advance and optional items were paid for in advance, so the basis is 439.83 - 161.88 - 12.95 = 265.00; 20 per cent of that is 53.00; Platinum's car rental discount of 8 per cent and a settlement of 439.83 against the relief figure of 300 reduce it to 48.76; the money settled works out at 73.30 a day, above the mid value figure of 60 and below the high value figure of 90, so the mid value multiple 1.05 gives 51.198; the booking was held twenty-six days, seven or more but under thirty, so the class's flat cancellation charge of 60.00 is added once; rounded once at the end, 111.20. Hand that to the renter to confirm. Then price the payout on the world as it now stands: the money settled in advance was collected in CAD, not the supplier's own currency, so it is taken as 439.83 less the class's 3.5 per cent conversion markup, 424.43595; the ledger now carries 111.20 as withheld and the vehicle was never collected, so exactly that is taken off; Platinum carries the agency-service-fee waiver and money has been settled in advance, so nothing is retained for the service element; one supplier message stands on the rental and her own travel protection stands issued on a declared trip of 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-15, which begins no later than the collection moment of 2026-10-07 and ends no earlier than the booked return of 2026-10-13, so 25 per cent of what is treated as withheld, 27.80, is put back; the optional items were sold on the booking date and the vehicle was never collected, so none of what was taken for them is kept; the figure is 341.03595, capped by neither nothing nor the 439.83 collected, and rounds once to 341.04.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN (Step 5). The computations were evaluated with the gate's own primitives (build_env / eval_compute from skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py) against initial_state at frozen_time, the charge tool was then executed on a seeded DB and the refund was evaluated against the resulting world. Output:
  drive_ext_cancellation_charge: result=111.2  (settled_in_advance_total=439.83, items_settled_total=161.88, notice_days=14, notice_band_pct=20, charge_basis=265.0, club_rental_discount_pct=8, member_relief_pct=8, day_rate_settled=73.305, value_multiple=1.05, days_held=26, holding_element=60.0, share_amount=53.0, after_relief=48.76, after_value=51.198)
    factor baselines: notice_band=264.79, charge_basis_measure=144.98, member_relief=115.65, value_band=108.76, holding_period_element=51.2; every one moves the result. All baselines at once = 351.86.
  drive_ext_cancellation_refund: result=341.04 (settled_in_advance_total=439.83, collection_currency=CAD, largest_settlement=439.83, settlement_count=1, returnable_settlement=424.43595, withheld_on_ledger=111.2, unavailability_notices=0, vehicle_collected_at='', withheld_applied=111.2, club_rental_discount_pct=8, fee_waiver_carried=True, retained_service_element=0.0, supplier_messages=1, cover_starts_by_days=2, cover_runs_to_days=2, protection_covers_rental=True, goodwill_put_back=27.8, items_settled_total=161.88, items_sold_date=2026-08-28, items_sold_after_booking_days=0, items_kept=0.0)
    factor baselines: settlement_measure=356.43, withholding_measure=94.56, service_element=328.09, supplier_message_goodwill=313.24, optional_items_kept=179.16; every one moves the result. All baselines at once = 0.0.
  prerequisite sensitivity: refund recomputed with the charge confirmation skipped = 424.44 against 341.04.
Both figures equal the gold arguments and the declared expected values exactly.

RULE/COMPUTE TWO-WAY SWEEP. Forward: every binding that reads the world, aggregates, chooses, crosses categories or rounds carries a verbatim quotation of the rule sentence that legislates it in compute_basis — the aggregates over the advance payment and the optional items, the two date spans, each of the five ladders in each policy, and the final rounding-and-cap sentence. Backward: reading each rule through, every load-bearing sentence is claimed — the notice-day counting rule (notice_days), the three notice bands (notice_band_pct), the three basis measures (charge_basis), the relief ladder (member_relief_pct), the value bands (value_multiple), the holding-period additions (holding_element), the rounding and order of assembly (result); and in the refund rule the settlement measures (returnable_settlement), the withholding measures (withheld_applied), the service element (retained_service_element), the goodwill ladder (goodwill_put_back), the items ladder (items_kept) and the floor, cap and rounding (result). The acting base is written out in prose in both rules (the share acts on the basis, the relief acts on the share, the value multiple acts on the reduced share, the holding element is added after the multiple and before the single rounding); the moment of the cap and the floor is written out in the refund rule (never less than nothing and never more than the money settled in advance, applied to the assembled figure before the single rounding); the interval conventions are written out (calendar days from date to date in both spans).

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Masking the extended YAML, compute, expected, gold and this dossier, and working only from what the published documents will say, the tool schemas, the rows the finders return and what the caller actually says: the caller asks for her money back on a cancelled rental; the refund document says the amount is worked out only after the ledger carries the charge withheld for the rental being given up; the ledger carries no such charge; the charge document gives a complete method and the records give every input; the confirmation of the charge is the renter's own act because the money is kept back from what she paid; the payout follows. The same two numbers come out, and no second reading of the documents produces another pair: the notice band, the basis, the relief, the value band and the holding element are each pinned to one tier by the records, and the refund's five factors likewise. The one place a careless reader diverges is the supplier message — treating it as a notice of unavailability yields 0.00 withheld and a refund of 424.44 — which is exactly the trap the reason code on that row is there to spring.

CLOSURE. policy -> target_tool -> computation -> GT call -> terminal state: drive_ext_cancellation_charge -> confirm_cancellation_charge_358c6472 -> computations[0] (step 7, cancellation_charge_usd = 111.2) -> the ledger row dce_... standing against the rental; drive_ext_cancellation_refund -> post_cancellation_refund_344e0f66 -> computations[1] (step 9, refund_amount_usd = 341.04) -> the payout row drf_... standing against the advance payment. charter_scope, required_documents and the computations' policy ids are the same two ids in the same order, and the gold calls exactly the two tools those policies name, in the topological order of the tree.


REWORK — ROUND 2, against env/online_travel_agency/audits/policy_task/car_rental_desk/0.md and _difficulty.md.
Every finding of the audit that bears on this task is answered below. No scored value moved: the charge is still 111.20, the payout still 341.04, every factor-sensitivity figure and both whole-baseline figures are unchanged, and the skip-effect is still 424.44. The re-run of the Step 5 verification after the changes reproduced all of them.

0-1 / F-1 (RED, undeclared override of "the agency service fee is not returned on any class"). CLOSED by declaring the override. `drive_ext_cancellation_refund.overwrite` now carries an entry naming `drive_cancellation`, quoting that clause verbatim as `superseded_clause`, and quoting this policy's own service-element ladder sentence as `replaced_by`. The override was always real and legal in substance — the club charter itself legislates `agency_service_fee_waiver` as a tier benefit — and it is now traceable clause by clause, so a reader of the merged policy knows which sentence yields and the payout has one defensible figure, 341.04. Base's other clauses of `drive_cancellation` stay in force and stay inherited; the declaration retires no eligibility gate (the superseded clause neither contains nor is contained in `inside_free_cancellation`'s condition), so `solvability_contract` is unchanged.

0-2 / F-3 (RED, the free-cancellation term's declared meaning against the rule that consumes it). CLOSED inside the write domain by giving the merged policy a tie-break that the extended policy — the version update, which wins where declared — states in its own rule: "The free-cancellation term of the rate class booked runs in whole elapsed hours from the moment the supplier confirmed the renter's booking, and not backwards from the scheduled collection moment; a rental given up inside that term has nothing withheld, and the charge worked out here is the one that arises outside it." That agrees with base `drive_cancellation`'s own sentence and with `inside_free_cancellation.temporal_basis` (anchor `drive_rentals.confirmed_at`, `elapsed_hours`, inclusive), so it is a restatement and not an override, and it needs no `overwrite` entry. It is deliberately not implemented as a compute branch: base counts the term "in whole elapsed hours from the confirmation moment, never mixing elapsed hours with calendar days", and the restricted expression language offers only whole-day arithmetic, so a computed guard would have had to invent a day-to-hour convention and would itself have contradicted that base sentence. The `parameter_schema` gloss that opens the second reading is part of the verbatim base copy and of `blueprint/products/drive.yaml`; base is frozen and was not touched. On this world the reading is now pinned: confirmation 2026-08-28 16:40 plus nought hours closes the term at that same moment, the cancellation at 2026-09-23 19:40 falls outside it, a charge is withheld, and the pair (111.20, 341.04) is the only defensible one.

0-3 (observation, the refund baseline floors at 0.00). ANSWERED, no change. The baseline is honest in the sense the gate and the skill require: every sentence of `baseline.rule` is verbatim in the rule, each factor's fall-through equals the baseline value for its input, and the paragraph yields a definite number from the records alone. Its fall-through for the withholding measure is the harshest reading — a computation document that is silent about whether the vehicle was collected must treat the whole of the money settled in advance as withheld — and the floor at nothing is base-compliant ("never less than nothing"). Every alternative considered either moved the scored payout or made a declared factor decorative: making the fall-through the ledger's charge would equal the tier this world takes and kill `withholding_measure`'s weight; inverting `optional_items_kept` would change the payout. The observation is recorded rather than engineered away.

0-4 (observation, the optional-items term subtracted from a base that never contained them). CLOSED by stating the composition of that base in both policies' rules: "The money settled in advance on a rental is the total of the advance payments taken on it, and it carries what was paid for the rental days, what was paid for any optional items bought in advance and the rate class's agency service fee." That is true of this world by construction — the single advance payment of 439.83 is exactly 265.00 of rental days plus 161.88 of optional items plus the 12.95 agency service fee — and it is now stated rather than presupposed, so both the charge policy's subtraction of the item money and the fee "so that the share acts on the rate alone", and the refund policy's keeping or returning of the item money, rest on a sentence the reader has. The sentence is claimed by `compute_basis.settled_in_advance_total` in both policies. No figure moves.

0-5 / F-4 (rule and compute part company on the goodwill factor's second tier). CLOSED by making the compute say what the rule says: the branch is now `supplier_messages == 1`, not `>= 1`, so the world with two or more messages and no qualifying condition falls through to "nothing is put back" exactly as the rule states. On this world one message stands, the tier is the same and the value is still 27.80.

0-6 / F-5 (two base sentences of `drive_refund_settlement` handled differently, undeclared). CLOSED by declaring both. `drive_ext_cancellation_refund.overwrite` now carries an entry superseding "Each payout is raised against the original ledger line it reverses, so a rental with several lines settles as several payouts and never as one lump sum." with this policy's new sentence "The amount returned is raised as one payout against the money the renter settled in advance, whatever the number of payments that money came in.", and a second entry superseding "A payout may never exceed the amount that original line actually collected" with the cap this policy states, "it is never less than nothing and never more than the money settled in advance". The remaining half of that base sentence — that the sum of a rental's payouts may never exceed its ledger total — is untouched and still inherited, and is satisfied here (341.04 against a ledger total of 601.71). Neither declaration retires an eligibility gate, so `rental_settled` is still inherited and still evidenced in `solvability_contract`.

0-7 (no finding on the derivation). Noted. The blind derivation reproduced every value; nothing in this rework moved any of them, and the Step 5 re-run confirms it figure for figure.

O-1 (ladders ordered rather than pairwise disjoint as stated). CLOSED in prose: each of this task's two policies now ends its rule with "Where more than one of the cases stated here fits a rental, the case stated earliest in this rule applies to that rental and the others do not." The convention the compute already implements is now legislated, so an overlapping pair of tiers can no longer be read two ways.

O-4 (`club` is a category without a difficulty of its own, so this task's cross-difficulty factors read no other difficulty's records). CLOSED by making the goodwill factor genuinely cross-difficulty on `care`, which is the `travel_protection_desk` difficulty. `supplier_message_goodwill` now tiers on the supplier's messages AND on whether the renter holds a travel protection policy in force over the rental period, read through `EXISTS('care', status='in_force')`; `cross_category` and `inputs.cross_category` declare `care` alongside `club`, and the world seeds the evidence — `care_policies/7ef9d876-935d-4ca4-8c6d-6fb0f4b98794`, a Trip Basics Standard for a spring journey, standing expired. The tier this world takes is unchanged (one message, no cover in force), so the goodwill element is still 27.80 and the payout still 341.04; the persona answers the question if the agent asks it and never volunteers it; and a read node, `find_care_policies`, now pulls the evidence into the reachable context. user_scenario:
Anneke Vorster is a 39-year-old procurement lead at a Calgary engineering firm who books her own travel and keeps a tidy folder of confirmations. She is polite, a little brisk, and slightly embarrassed about the whole business, because the Denver trip she had planned for October fell through when the project she was flying down for was pushed to the spring. She gave the car up in the Wanderlane app last night, saw the booking flip to cancelled, and is calling the morning after about her money: she paid the whole rental up front back in August, on her Canadian card, and what she wants to know is what comes back to that card and to have it actually set moving today rather than left sitting. She is happy for the desk to do whatever it has to do on its side; she is not asking anyone to reverse the cancellation, and she is not asking about the trip being rebooked, since the new dates are nowhere near settled.

She opens with her name, Anneke Vorster, and the mobile number the booking notifications go to, 7040318294, because that is what she always gets asked for. If the agent needs more before discussing the account she reads her date of birth off her passport as 1987-03-14 and the last four characters of the passport number as 4472; she has her billing postcode to hand too but only offers it if the first two are not enough. The rental agreement number is RA7431902 if it is wanted, and she will say the car was a standard-size one out of the downtown Denver branch, collected the seventh of October and back on the thirteenth, if she is asked to confirm which booking is being discussed. She does not remember exactly what she paid, and if she is pressed on the figure she says she would rather the agent read it off the booking than have her guess from a card statement in another currency; she does remember there was a child seat and a satellite navigation unit on it for her sister, who was to drive part of the way.

She has a Wanderlane card and mentions it only if the agent asks whether she is a member, in which case she says she has been Platinum since the winter and reads the membership number WL-7742-0318. She will not claim any particular benefit from it: as far as she is concerned that is the desk's business, not hers. Asked whether she had any travel cover for the Denver trip, she says she did put a TripGuard policy on it through Wanderlane the same afternoon she booked the car, certificate TG-2026-771903, and that it runs from the fifth to the fifteenth of October; there is an older one on her account from a trip in the spring, long finished, which she mentions only so the agent is not surprised by it. Whether either of them has anything to do with what comes back on the car she has no idea, she is not asking anybody here to make a claim for her, and she leaves that side of it with the desk.

She does not know, and never raises, anything about what the terms keep back when a rental is given up. If the agent explains that giving the car up this far out carries a charge that is kept back out of what she paid, she takes it without arguing — she says she expected something to be held back — and when the agent hands the confirmation over to her and asks her to put it through herself, she does it there and then and reads back whatever the system tells her. Should the agent ask her to confirm that she is content for the charge to come out of the money she already paid rather than be billed separately, she says yes, that is what she would prefer. If instead the agent tells her nothing at all is being held back, she does not contradict it; she only says that seems generous and waits to hear what she is getting.

Once the agent tells her the money has been raised back to the card, she asks only how long it usually takes to land and, whatever she is told, thanks them and rings off. If she is told a figure that is obviously less than she expected she will say, once, that it does not feel like much against what she paid in August and ask that it be checked against the booking, but she cannot say what it ought to be and will accept the second answer either way. She never pushes for a particular number, never quotes a rule, and if the agent misses something she has no idea of it.

If the agent asks anything she cannot answer from her own papers — where the supplier is in its own processing, what the branch did with the vehicle afterwards, whether anyone has looked at the message the supplier sent her in September about the rate on the booking — she says plainly that she has no way of knowing and leaves it with the desk. Her only hard preference is that whatever comes back goes to the card she paid with; she has no interest in credit, a voucher or a future booking.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never names the prerequisite problem, the charge it books or anything owed on the rental. The caller speaks only about her money coming back to her card, her trip falling through, her identity details, her membership when asked, and a supplier message she cannot explain. She asks no question of the form 'is anything held back?' and drops no hint that something must be sorted out first; her only contribution on that side is the passive branch in which, after the agent has explained that a charge is kept back and handed the confirmation to her, she puts it through herself.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: Neither tool validates the prerequisite. post_cancellation_refund_344e0f66 consists of one ctx.make_id and one ctx.create: it does not read the ledger, does not look for a cancellation charge, does not test the rental's status and returns no policy-based error, so it books whatever amount it is given whether or not the charge line stands. confirm_cancellation_charge_358c6472 is the same shape and equally unguarded. The consequence of leaving the prerequisite unresolved appears only as a different terminal hash.

factor_trace: notice_band (parameter): evidence is the rental's own dates - cancelled_at 2026-09-23 and pickup_at 2026-10-07 give notice_days 14, exactly on the fourteen-or-more boundary, so the ladder's first tier applies and the share is 20 per cent. Baseline: the computation document's standing share of eighty per cent, which would have given 264.79.

charge_basis_measure (method): evidence is the rental's ledger - the advance payment 738d4229 of 439.83 and the two optional-item lines 8b6db416 (83.94) and 62d80f88 (77.94) summing to 161.88, so money has been settled in advance and items were also paid for in advance and the first tier applies: the basis is 439.83 - 161.88 - 12.95 = 265.00. Baseline: the standard method takes the basis as the whole of the money settled in advance, 439.83, which would have given 144.98.

member_relief (parameter, cross-difficulty on club): evidence is the membership row e5a2e01d standing active at Wanderlane Platinum, whose car rental discount of 8 per cent is at least the relief threshold of 5, together with the money settled in advance of 439.83 against the relief settlement figure of 300, so the first tier applies and the share is reduced by 8 per cent. Baseline: no relief, which would have given 115.65.

value_band (parameter): evidence is the money settled in advance over the charged days, 439.83 / 6 = 73.30 a day, above the mid value figure of 60 and not above the high value figure of 90, so the second tier applies and the multiple is 1.05. Baseline: a multiple of one, which would have given 108.76.

holding_period_element (parameter): evidence is the rental's booked_date 2026-08-28 against cancelled_at 2026-09-23, twenty-six days held, seven or more but under thirty, so the second tier applies and the class's flat cancellation charge of 60.00 is added once. Baseline: nothing added, which would have given 51.2.

bindings belonging to no factor: settled_in_advance_total (the 439.83 advance payment, read straight off the ledger), share_amount, after_relief and after_value (the assembly of the basis, the share, the relief and the multiple in the order the rule states) and result (the single rounding at the end).

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: fourteen or more whole days of notice were given between the rental being given up and the scheduled collection
money has been settled in advance on the rental and optional items have also been paid for in advance

the renter holds an active club membership whose tier carries a car rental discount of at least the relief threshold and the money settled in advance on the rental reaches the relief settlement figure
the money settled in advance works out at more than the mid value figure for each charged rental day
the renter held the booking for seven days or more before giving it up

factor_trace: settlement_measure (method): evidence is the advance payment line 738d4229, whose currency_charged is CAD and which is the only payment of its kind on the rental, so the first tier applies and the money settled in advance is taken as 439.83 less the class's 3.5 per cent conversion markup, 424.43595. Baseline: the whole of what was collected, 439.83, which would have given 356.43.

withholding_measure (method): evidence is the count of supplier messages saying the vehicle cannot be provided, which is nil - the one message 659040c6 carries the reason of a rate correction - together with the rental's empty collection moment, so the second tier applies and exactly the 111.20 the ledger now carries for the rental being given up is treated as withheld. Baseline: the whole of the money settled in advance treated as withheld, which would have given 94.56.

service_element (parameter, cross-difficulty on club): evidence is the membership row e5a2e01d standing active at Wanderlane Platinum, whose tier carries the waiver of the agency service fee, together with money settled in advance on the rental, so the first tier applies and nothing is retained. Baseline: the rate class's agency service fee of 12.95 retained, which would have given 328.09.

supplier_message_goodwill (parameter, cross-difficulty on care): evidence is the single supplier message 659040c6 standing on the rental together with the renter's own travel protection - policy 09532a38 stands issued on a declared trip running 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-15, which begins two days before the collection moment and ends two days after the booked return, so it spans the rental; the second policy on file, 7ef9d876, declares a spring trip and stands expired, and is excluded on both counts. The second tier therefore applies and 25 per cent of what is treated as withheld, 27.80, is put back. Baseline: nothing put back, which would have given 313.24. Withdraw the issued policy, expire it, or move its declared trip off the rental and the tier falls through: the payout becomes 313.24.

optional_items_kept (parameter): evidence is the two optional-item lines totalling 161.88 and the latest of their posting dates, 2026-08-28, which is the day the rental was booked, together with the rental's empty collection moment, so the first tier applies and none of what was taken for them is kept. Baseline: the whole of what was taken for them kept, which would have given 179.16.

bindings belonging to no factor: settled_in_advance_total (the 439.83 advance payment), withheld_on_ledger (the charge the prerequisite write put on the ledger, 111.2, which is 0.0 until it lands) and result (the floor at nothing, the cap at the money settled in advance, and the single rounding).
